playbooks.name: Operation Midnight Strike
playbooks.description: A state-sponsored intrusion beginning with a macro-enabled invoice document delivered to the finance team. The operator pivots from Office to encoded PowerShell, injects into a trusted host process, dumps LSASS for credential material, and reuses harvested domain administrator hashes to move laterally over SMB administrative shares.

techniques.description: A finance analyst opens a macro-enabled invoice attachment delivered by email. The document's VBA project spawns a hidden, base64-encoded PowerShell stager from WINWORD.EXE.
reference_indicators: ParentImage ends with 'WINWORD.EXE'
CommandLine contains '-Enc' (base64-encoded payload)
CommandLine contains '-W Hidden' (suppressed window)
Security EID 4688 NewProcessName: powershell.exe spawned by an Office application
ParentCommandLine references a .docm opened from the Outlook Content.Outlook cache
red_herring_indicators: IntegrityLevel: Medium (process is running elevated)
TokenElevationType: %%1936 (full administrator token)
Sysmon EID 11 TargetFilename: ~WRD0001.tmp (Word autosave artifact)
CurrentDirectory: C:\Users\jdoe\Documents\ (unusual working directory)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Office Application Spawning Encoded PowerShell
id: 67cd2477-6f8b-49a5-ab26-03f5b4dd7ad4
status: experimental
description: Detects a Microsoft Office application spawning PowerShell with an encoded command line, a common spearphishing attachment execution chain.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\WINWORD.EXE'
      - '\EXCEL.EXE'
      - '\POWERPNT.EXE'
      - '\OUTLOOK.EXE'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -Enc'
      - ' -EncodedCommand'
      - ' -W Hidden'
      - ' -WindowStyle Hidden'
  filter_legitimate:
    CommandLine|contains: '\Program Files\Microsoft Office\Updates\'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_flags and not filter_legitimate
falsepositives:
  - Office add-in deployment scripts executed by IT automation
level: high
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1566.001
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.001

techniques.description: The stager relaunches PowerShell with execution policy bypassed and a second encoded payload that pulls the implant from the operator's staging host over HTTP.
reference_indicators: CommandLine contains '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
CommandLine contains '-enc' (base64-encoded command)
CommandLine contains '-NoProfile'
Decoded payload contains 'Invoke-WebRequest' to an external host
Sysmon EID 3 powershell.exe initiated an outbound connection to 185.220.101.47
red_herring_indicators: SubjectLogonId: 0x4a91c (SYSTEM logon session)
DestinationPort: 80 (standard web traffic, no action needed)
OriginalFileName: PowerShell.EXE (renamed binary detected)
TokenElevationType: %%1938 (limited token indicates UAC bypass)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect PowerShell Execution Policy Bypass With Encoded Command
id: 8abe0c64-31a8-4b0b-8783-8a75a51aaa81
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell invoked with both an execution policy bypass and a base64 encoded command, a hallmark of staged implant delivery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_bypass:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
      - '-ep bypass'
      - '-exec bypass'
  selection_encoded:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -enc '
      - ' -EncodedCommand '
      - ' -e JAB'
  filter_sccm:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\CcmExec.exe'
  condition: selection_image and selection_bypass and selection_encoded and not filter_sccm
falsepositives:
  - Software distribution platforms that wrap encoded install scripts
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.001

techniques.description: The implant is written to disk as a DLL, mapped into the user's explorer.exe session, and executed via a remote thread so that subsequent activity originates from a trusted, signed process.
reference_indicators: Sysmon EID 8 CreateRemoteThread SourceImage: powershell.exe
Sysmon EID 8 TargetImage: explorer.exe
Sysmon EID 10 GrantedAccess: 0x1fffff (PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS)
StartAddress 0x7ffb3a210000 has no backing module (StartModule is empty)
Sysmon EID 7 unsigned DLL loaded from AppData\Local\Temp
red_herring_indicators: Sysmon EID 8 NewThreadId: 4820 (thread identifier outside the valid range)
TargetImage explorer.exe is a signed Microsoft binary
CallTrace begins in ntdll.dll (kernel transition, always malicious)
SourceUser and TargetUser are identical (privilege escalation confirmed)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Remote Thread Injection Into Explorer From Script Host
id: 257d6b2e-3c73-430f-9b7f-fecf8c1ce7ad
status: experimental
description: Detects a scripting host creating a remote thread in a trusted shell process with full access rights, indicating DLL or shellcode injection.
references:

author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: create_remote_thread
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    SourceImage|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
    TargetImage|endswith:
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\svchost.exe'
      - '\dllhost.exe'
  filter_known_module:
    StartModule|contains: 'C:\Windows\System32\'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_module
falsepositives:
  - Endpoint agents performing in-memory instrumentation
level: high
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1055.001

techniques.description: Running inside explorer.exe, the implant opens a handle to LSASS with read and query rights and writes a process minidump to the user temp directory for offline credential extraction.
reference_indicators: Sysmon EID 10 TargetImage: lsass.exe
Sysmon EID 10 GrantedAccess: 0x1010
CallTrace contains UNKNOWN unbacked memory region
Security EID 4656 AccessMask: 0x1010 against lsass.exe
Sysmon EID 11 TargetFilename: lsass.dmp written to AppData\Local\Temp
red_herring_indicators: SubjectUserName: svc_backup (backup service accounts may read process memory)
TargetUser: NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (LSASS always runs as SYSTEM)
ObjectServer: Security (audit subsystem, benign)
SourceImage: explorer.exe is a signed Microsoft shell binary
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect LSASS Memory Access via Process Access
id: fa46aa29-eaef-466e-9f81-65b1c0c5bb28
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious access to LSASS process memory indicating credential dumping.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25

  category: process_access
  product: windows

    TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    GrantedAccess|contains:
      - '0x1010'

  filter_legitimate:
    SourceImage|contains:
      - 'MsMpEng.exe'

techniques.description: Hashes recovered from the LSASS dump are replayed against the domain controller. A domain administrator authenticates over the network with NTLM from the compromised finance workstation, followed by an RC4-encrypted Kerberos ticket request.

fields.PrivilegeList: SeSecurityPrivilege SeBackupPrivilege SeRestorePrivilege SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege SeDebugPrivilege SeImpersonatePrivilege

reference_indicators: Security EID 4624 LogonType: 3 (network logon)
AuthenticationPackageName: NTLM used for a domain administrator logon
TargetUserName: CORP\domain_admin authenticating from a finance workstation
Security EID 4769 TicketEncryptionType: 0x17 (RC4-HMAC downgrade)
IpAddress: 10.10.10.88 matches the previously compromised host
red_herring_indicators: LogonProcessName: NtLmSsp (unrecognised logon provider)
Security EID 4769 ServiceName: krbtgt (unusual service principal)
KeyLength: 128 (weak session key negotiated)
Security EID 4672 SeBackupPrivilege assigned (backup operator activity)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect NTLM Network Logon For Privileged Account From Workstation
id: 4a77c32f-63a4-4b1a-bd75-593e5b5c3a76
status: experimental
description: Detects a privileged domain account performing an NTLM network logon sourced from an end-user workstation, consistent with pass-the-hash lateral movement.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
    AuthenticationPackageName: 'NTLM'
    TargetUserName|contains:
      - 'domain_admin'
      - 'ent_admin'
      - '_adm'
  filter_workstation:
    WorkstationName|startswith:
      - 'SRV-'
      - 'DC-'
      - 'MGMT-'
  condition: selection and not filter_workstation
falsepositives:
  - Legacy applications that still negotiate NTLM for administrative tasks
level: high
tags:
  - attack.lateral_movement
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1078

techniques.description: With domain administrator context, the operator connects to the ADMIN$ share on a file server, drops a service binary, and registers it to obtain remote execution.
reference_indicators: Security EID 5140 ShareName: \\*\ADMIN$ accessed remotely
Security EID 7045 new service installed: PSEXESVC
Sysmon EID 3 outbound TCP/445 initiated to 10.10.10.92
SubjectUserName: domain_admin originating from 10.10.10.88
Service ImagePath resolves to %SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe
red_herring_indicators: Sysmon EID 3 Image: svchost.exe (signed Microsoft service host)
ShareLocalPath: C:\Windows (non-standard share target)
AccessMask: 0x1 (read access only, low risk)
AccountName: LocalSystem (service accounts always run as LocalSystem)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Remote Service Installation Following Admin Share Access
id: 0a07493c-7ca4-457b-b29a-7a7c745a9e0d
status: experimental
description: Detects installation of a remote execution service such as PSEXESVC, typically preceded by access to the ADMIN$ administrative share.

  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25

      - '%SystemRoot%\'

level: high
tags:
  - attack.lateral_movement
  - attack.t1021.002

playbooks.name: LockBit Ransomware Kill Chain
playbooks.description: An affiliate exploits an internet-facing CMS plugin to gain code execution on a DMZ web server, establishes registry run-key persistence while disabling Defender, destroys shadow copies and recovery options, encrypts user data, and beacons the collected files to the affiliate's C2 infrastructure.

techniques.description: An unauthenticated file-upload flaw in a CMS admin AJAX endpoint is abused from a scripted client to write a PHP handler into the web root and trigger an outbound callback.
reference_indicators: HTTP POST to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=upload_file returned 200
user_agent: python-requests/2.28.0 (scripted client, not a browser)
Sysmon EID 3 w3wp.exe initiated an outbound connection to 203.0.113.45
Sysmon EID 11 new .php file written under C:\inetpub\wwwroot by w3wp.exe
Inbound request and outbound callback share the same external IP
red_herring_indicators: status: 200 (request completed successfully, therefore authorised)
bytes: 4096 (standard response size)
s_port: 443 (traffic was encrypted in transit)
cs_username: '-' (anonymous access is normal for public sites)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Web Server Process Writing Executable Web Content
id: b148f197-e7a9-426f-947e-f372b370584a
status: experimental
description: Detects an IIS worker process writing server-side script files into the web root, the typical outcome of exploiting a public-facing upload flaw.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\inetpub\wwwroot\'
      - '\wwwroot\'
      - '\htdocs\'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.aspx'
      - '.asp'
      - '.jsp'
  filter_deploy:
    Image|endswith: '\msdeploy.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_deploy
falsepositives:
  - Content management systems performing in-place plugin updates
level: high
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190

techniques.description: The planted PHP handler is invoked to run cmd.exe under the IIS application pool identity, performing quick identity and network reconnaissance on the compromised host.
reference_indicators: ParentProcessName: w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe
CommandLine contains 'whoami' (identity reconnaissance)
CommandLine contains 'ipconfig /all' (network reconnaissance)
User: IIS APPPOOL\DefaultAppPool executing an interactive shell
Command chaining with '&&' from a web tier process
red_herring_indicators: CurrentDirectory: C:\Windows\system32\inetsrv\ (suspicious working directory)
IntegrityLevel: High (proof of privilege escalation)
OriginalFileName: Cmd.Exe (binary has been renamed)
SubjectLogonId: 0x3e5 (interactive console session)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Command Shell Spawned By IIS Worker Process
id: 6ddec96d-0419-44d1-96f0-c6cba7fc3d39
status: experimental
description: Detects cmd.exe or PowerShell launched by the IIS worker process, indicating web shell or exploitation driven command execution.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'

      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'

    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'whoami'

  - attack.t1059.003

techniques.description: The payload is staged in C:\ProgramData and registered under the machine Run key so it survives reboot, while a second registry write disables Defender's real-time anti-spyware protection.
reference_indicators: Sysmon EID 13 TargetObject: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\SystemUpdater
Registry Details point to C:\ProgramData\lockbit.exe
Sysmon EID 13 SetValue on Windows Defender DisableAntiSpyware
Sysmon EID 11 executable written to C:\ProgramData by cmd.exe
Run key value name 'SystemUpdater' masquerades as a Windows component
red_herring_indicators: EventType: SetValue (all registry writes use SetValue)
User: NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (trusted built-in account, benign)
TargetObject is under HKLM (machine hive access is routine)
Details: DWORD (0x00000001) (a value of 1 always means enabled)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Run Key Persistence And Defender Tampering
id: 93d5b8b5-7b31-4bf7-b26f-615d57608e9d
status: experimental
description: Detects registry writes that create autorun persistence from a non-standard program directory or disable Microsoft Defender protection features.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1112/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: registry_set
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_runkey:
    TargetObject|contains: '\CurrentVersion\Run\'
    Details|contains:
      - 'C:\ProgramData\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - 'C:\Users\Public\'
  selection_defender:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware'
      - '\Real-Time Protection\DisableRealtimeMonitoring'
    Details: 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
  filter_installer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
  condition: (selection_runkey or selection_defender) and not filter_installer
falsepositives:
  - Vendor installers that stage components in ProgramData
level: high
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1112

techniques.description: Immediately before encryption the operator deletes every volume shadow copy and disables Windows recovery, removing the victim's ability to roll back.
reference_indicators: CommandLine: vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet
vssadmin.exe spawned by cmd.exe rather than an administrative console
CommandLine: bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No
ParentCommandLine references C:\ProgramData\lockbit.exe --prepare
Shadow copy deletion uses /quiet to suppress operator confirmation
red_herring_indicators: NewProcessName: vssadmin.exe (unsigned third-party binary)
ParentProcessName: cmd.exe (standard command interpreter, expected)
IntegrityLevel: System (normal for scheduled maintenance jobs)
SubjectLogonId: 0x3e7 (SYSTEM session, always trustworthy)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Shadow Copy Deletion And Recovery Tampering
id: f8da0872-84bd-4b24-bad1-20da8a5ca8eb
status: experimental
description: Detects destruction of volume shadow copies or disabling of Windows recovery, a precursor to ransomware encryption.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_vss:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\vssadmin.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'delete shadows'
      - 'shadowcopy delete'
  selection_bcd:
    Image|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'recoveryenabled No'
      - 'bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures'
  filter_backup:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\VeeamBackupSvc.exe'
  condition: (selection_vss or selection_bcd) and not filter_backup
falsepositives:
  - Backup products pruning their own shadow copies
level: critical
tags:
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1490

techniques.description: The payload walks user profile directories, rewrites documents with a .locked extension and drops a ransom note in every traversed folder.
reference_indicators: Sysmon EID 11 file creation with a .locked extension
Image: C:\ProgramData\lockbit.exe writing into user document folders
Ransom note '!!!-Restore-My-Files-!!!.txt' created on the user Desktop
Security EID 4663 AccessMask: 0x2 (WriteData) across C:\Users\jdoe\Documents\
A single process rewriting many files in rapid succession
red_herring_indicators: SubjectUserName: SYSTEM (the operating system wrote these files)
ObjectName: C:\Users\jdoe\Documents\ (standard user profile folder)
ObjectServer: Security (audit subsystem entry, informational)
HandleId: 0x9c4 (handle value outside the expected range)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Mass File Rename To Ransomware Extension
id: fd39aacc-2b44-4a6f-8180-6a4d519ebebf
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of files with known ransomware extensions alongside ransom note filenames in user profile directories.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ext:

  - attack.t1486

techniques.description: Collected documents are shipped to the affiliate's leak-site staging server over the same channel the implant already uses for tasking, supporting the double-extortion model.
reference_indicators: Sysmon EID 1 CommandLine contains '--exfil --host 185.220.101.47'
Sysmon EID 3 outbound TCP/443 initiated by C:\ProgramData\lockbit.exe
DestinationIp 185.220.101.47 is not a sanctioned corporate destination
Exfiltration reuses the same host the implant beacons to
A non-browser binary in ProgramData establishing TLS-port egress
red_herring_indicators: DestinationPort: 443 (standard HTTPS traffic, therefore benign)
Protocol: tcp (normal transport protocol)
DestinationHostname: '-' (name resolution succeeded)
SourceIp: 10.20.30.15 (internal address, traffic stayed on the LAN)

playbooks.name: Silent Web Breach & Data Exfiltration
playbooks.description: A quiet, low-and-slow intrusion. The actor exploits an internet-facing application, plants an ASPX web shell for durable access, harvests a database connection string from web.config, authenticates to the SQL tier with the stolen service account, dumps the customer table, and uploads it to a public file-sharing service outside the C2 channel.

techniques.description: A scripted client abuses an unauthenticated upload endpoint on the external marketing site, achieving arbitrary file write in the IIS web root.
reference_indicators: HTTP POST to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=upload_file returned 200
user_agent: python-requests/2.28.0 indicates automated exploitation
Sysmon EID 3 w3wp.exe initiated an outbound connection to 198.51.100.77
A 403 probe from the same src_ip immediately precedes the successful POST
Web tier process performing outbound egress on a non-standard port
red_herring_indicators: uri contains '/wp-admin/' (routine administrator activity)
time_taken: 812 ms (abnormally slow response indicates DoS)
status: 403 on the first request (the attack was blocked)
SourceIp: 10.30.40.11 (internal address, no external exposure)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Scripted Exploitation Of Public Upload Endpoint
id: ab1c7cdd-7a77-483d-94c9-ebd0622a5bac
status: experimental
description: Detects non-browser user agents posting to administrative upload endpoints followed by outbound egress from the web worker process.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: webserver
  product: iis
detection:
  selection_request:
    cs_method: 'POST'
    cs_uri_stem|contains:
      - '/admin-ajax.php'
      - '/upload'
      - '/fileupload'
    sc_status: 200
  selection_agent:
    cs_user_agent|contains:
      - 'python-requests'
      - 'curl/'
      - 'Go-http-client'
      - 'sqlmap'
  filter_monitoring:
    c_ip|startswith: '10.30.40.'
  condition: selection_request and selection_agent and not filter_monitoring
falsepositives:
  - Internal integration jobs that post files using scripted HTTP clients
level: high
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190

techniques.description: An ASPX web shell is written into the uploads directory, giving the actor durable command execution that survives reboots and does not depend on the original exploit.
reference_indicators: Sysmon EID 11 .aspx file written into C:\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\
w3wp.exe wrote server-side executable web content at runtime
Security EID 4688 cmd.exe spawned by w3wp.exe
CommandLine: cmd.exe /c dir C:\Users (filesystem enumeration from the web tier)
Command execution occurs minutes after the file write, from the same worker process
red_herring_indicators: TargetFilename resides under C:\inetpub\wwwroot (the normal web root, expected)
Image: w3wp.exe (signed IIS worker process, therefore trusted)
IntegrityLevel: High (routine for application pool identities)
OriginalFileName: Cmd.Exe (the binary was renamed to evade detection)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect ASPX Web Shell Drop In IIS Upload Directory
id: 48c5850d-05d1-4dc9-9acf-4ac5eab617e2
status: experimental
description: Detects the IIS worker process creating an ASPX or ASHX file in an upload directory, the classic web shell persistence artefact.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.aspx'
      - '.ashx'
      - '.asmx'
      - '.asp'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\uploads\'
      - '\temp\'
      - '\images\'
      - '\App_Data\'
  filter_publish:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\App_Data\_deploy\'
  condition: selection and selection_path and not filter_publish
falsepositives:
  - Application deployment that writes views into a staging upload path
level: critical
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003

techniques.description: Through the web shell the actor reads the application's web.config and filters it for connection strings, recovering a plaintext SQL service account password.
reference_indicators: CommandLine reads web.config and filters for 'connectionString'
Security EID 4663 ReadData (0x1) on C:\inetpub\wwwroot\web.config
Configuration file accessed by IIS APPPOOL\DefaultAppPool via cmd.exe
findstr.exe launched as a child of the web shell command chain
Credential material searched for immediately after web shell deployment
red_herring_indicators: AccessMask: 0x1 (read access is non-destructive, no risk)
ObjectName ends with .config (routine configuration read)
Image: findstr.exe (a signed Microsoft utility, therefore benign)
SubjectLogonId: 0x3e5 (LOCAL SERVICE session, expected for IIS)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Configuration File Credential Harvesting
id: 6824d70e-d90b-4350-927c-9e4d1d3dbd77
status: experimental
description: Detects command line reads of application configuration files filtered for credential keywords, indicating credentials in files harvesting.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_file:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'web.config'
      - 'appsettings.json'
      - 'unattend.xml'
      - '.aws\credentials'
  selection_keyword:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'connectionString'
      - 'password'
      - 'findstr'
      - 'Select-String'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  filter_admin:
    User|contains: 'CORP\svc_deploy'
  condition: selection_file and selection_keyword and selection_parent and not filter_admin
falsepositives:
  - Deployment scripts validating connection strings after release
level: high
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001

techniques.description: The harvested service account is replayed against the database server. Because the logon uses valid credentials it blends into normal authentication traffic, and the account is granted debug and ownership privileges it never needed.
reference_indicators: Security EID 4624 LogonType: 3 using credentials recovered from web.config
TargetUserName: CORP\svc_sqlreport authenticating from the DMZ web server
Security EID 4672 SeDebugPrivilege granted to a reporting service account
Logon occurred at 03:14, outside the account's normal baseline window
WorkstationName: WEB-EXT-11 is an internet-facing host, not an admin console
red_herring_indicators: AuthenticationPackageName: NTLM (an unsupported legacy protocol)
KeyLength: 128 (weak key negotiated, cryptographic downgrade)
TargetDomainName: CORP (logon crossed a domain trust boundary)
IpPort: 50942 (ephemeral source port indicates spoofing)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Service Account Logon From DMZ Web Server
id: 9ea2c9c5-3a54-4015-9c24-6d8265365357
status: experimental
description: Detects service account network logons sourced from internet-facing web servers, a strong signal of stolen credential reuse after web compromise.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
    TargetUserName|startswith: 'CORP\svc_'
    WorkstationName|startswith:
      - 'WEB-EXT-'
      - 'WEB-DMZ-'
  selection_priv:
    EventID: 4672
    PrivilegeList|contains: 'SeDebugPrivilege'
  filter_healthcheck:
    TargetUserName: 'CORP\svc_monitor'
  condition: (selection or selection_priv) and not filter_healthcheck
falsepositives:
  - Application pools configured to reach internal services with a domain identity
level: high
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1078

techniques.description: Using the stolen service account the actor runs sqlcmd against the local database instance and stages the entire customer table as a CSV in a temporary directory.

fields.CommandLine: sqlcmd -S localhost -U db_admin -P ******** -Q "SELECT * FROM dbo.customers INTO OUTFILE 'C:\Temp\dump.csv'"
fields.ParentCommandLine: cmd.exe /c sqlcmd -S localhost -U db_admin -P ******** -Q "SELECT * FROM dbo.customers"

reference_indicators: CommandLine contains 'SELECT * FROM dbo.customers' (bulk table read)
Plaintext credentials passed on the sqlcmd command line via -U and -P
Security EID 4663 WriteData (0x2) creating C:\Temp\dump.csv
Database export written to a non-standard staging directory
sqlcmd.exe executed under svc_sqlreport by a cmd.exe parent, not an agent job
red_herring_indicators: Image: sqlcmd.exe (a legitimate Microsoft SQL utility, therefore benign)
ObjectName: C:\Temp\dump.csv (temporary directory usage is routine)
IntegrityLevel: High (SQL tooling always runs elevated)
CurrentDirectory: C:\Temp\ (default working directory for sqlcmd)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect Bulk Database Export To Local Staging File
id: 449c777e-530e-4326-afb4-21a9204e9f7b
status: experimental
description: Detects command line database clients performing unbounded table selects redirected to a local file, indicating collection of local system data.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\sqlcmd.exe'
      - '\bcp.exe'
      - '\osql.exe'
      - '\mysql.exe'
  selection_query:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'SELECT * FROM'
      - 'INTO OUTFILE'
      - 'bcp '
  selection_output:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'C:\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - 'C:\Users\Public\'
      - '.csv'
  filter_agent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\sqlagent.exe'
  condition: selection_tool and selection_query and selection_output and not filter_agent
falsepositives:
  - Scheduled reporting exports run by database administrators
level: high
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1005

techniques.description: The staged CSV is uploaded with the built-in curl client to a public file-sharing service, deliberately separate from any command and control channel so that C2 blocking alone would not stop the data loss.
reference_indicators: curl.exe uploading C:\Temp\dump.csv with the -T (file transfer) flag
DestinationHostname file.io is an unapproved public file-sharing service
Sysmon EID 3 curl.exe connecting outbound to 45.33.32.156:443
Bearer token embedded in the command line for a third-party upload API
Exfiltration channel is distinct from any established C2 session
red_herring_indicators: DestinationPort: 443 (encrypted transport, therefore trusted)
Image: curl.exe (built into Windows since 1803, always benign)
IntegrityLevel: High (required for any network client)
SourceIp: 10.40.50.22 (RFC1918 address, traffic never left the network)
techniques.sigma_rule_yaml:
title: Detect File Upload To Public Sharing Service via curl
id: 5d042ae2-348c-4b6e-bc13-10e34918056a
status: experimental
description: Detects the built-in curl client uploading local files to known public file sharing services, indicating exfiltration over an alternative non-C2 protocol.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/003/
author: BlackPerl DFIR
date: 2026/07/25
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
  selection_upload:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -T '
      - ' --upload-file'
      - ' -F file@'
  selection_dest:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'file.io'
      - 'transfer.sh'
      - 'anonfiles.com'
      - 'pastebin.com'
      - 'temp.sh'
  filter_internal:
    CommandLine|contains: 'https://artifacts.corp.internal'
  condition: selection_tool and selection_upload and selection_dest and not filter_internal
falsepositives:
  - Developers sharing build artefacts through public paste services
level: critical
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1048.003
